role.altitude: The adult education teacher keeps planning programmes with colleagues, meeting other professionals and counselling learners; drafting module texts, taking minutes and gathering learners' attendance and results shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted module texts against the learners' language level
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spots a learner drifting away in week two, not week six.

tasks.short: Meet the team to plan the programme, draft module descriptions and lesson sequences, collect and share materials, and review colleagues' parts, collaborating in the development of instructional programs.

steps.what: Adult education teacher collaborates with other teachers and professionals in planning meetings for the instructional program
Adult education teacher drafts module descriptions, learning goals by language level and the lesson sequence

loop.input: The agreed programme outline, the target language level and the school's module template.
loop.output: Draft module descriptions with goals and a lesson sequence in the template.
loop.check: Every goal must match a descriptor of the target level from the school's goal list, or it is marked; the teacher reads each goal and lesson step against the descriptor's meaning and the agreed outline and edits all text before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft per module; after two redrafts the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template gives headings; the content differs per group and level.

steps.what: Adult education teacher collects and shares materials with colleagues by mail
Adult education teacher reviews colleagues' parts and gives feedback

tasks.design: Planning with colleagues stays in meetings. A bounded step drafts module descriptions and lesson sequences in the school's template from the agreed outline, checking goals against the school's list for the target language level; the teacher edits. Materials sit in one shared programme folder instead of mail attachments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Module texts were written from scratch and materials went round by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Course tools that turn outlines and documents into first drafts.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing what a mixed-level group needs.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what adult learners will actually practise at home.
tasks.altitude: A little less writing; programme choices stay with the team.

evidence.claim: A Dutch course tool turns documents or slide decks into a first course draft.
Drafting course material is not an AI Act high-risk use; evaluating learners is.

assumptions: Boundary: developing the programme; teaching it is outside.
Input contract for s2: the school's module template and its list of goals per language level, kept by the team leader.
Meetings and reviews keep their full time.
research_questions: How much drafted text survives the team's review?

already_counted.description: Adult education teacher edits drafted module texts.

incremental.description: Adult education teacher keeps the shared folder in order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small revisions to an existing programme, so drafts help little (s2 at 90) and materials are already shared (s3 at 95) (3.4); high: a new programme with many modules (10.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the agenda and papers, attend staff meetings and serve on committees, take minutes when it is one's turn and follow up action points.

steps.what: Adult education teacher reads the agenda and meeting papers
Adult education teacher attends staff meetings and serves on committees
Adult education teacher takes and writes up the minutes when it is their turn

loop.input: The meeting transcript, recorded with all attendees' consent, and the agenda.
loop.output: Draft minutes per agenda item with decisions and action points with owners.
loop.check: Every decision and action point must point to a moment in the transcript, or it is marked; the minute-taker edits and the chair agrees the minutes before they are shared.
loop.why_not_simpler: The agenda gives items; decisions come out of the discussion.

steps.what: Adult education teacher checks the minutes before they are shared: decisions, owners and action points as the chair agreed
Adult education teacher shares the checked minutes with the meeting's members
Adult education teacher follows up their own action points

tasks.design: Meetings and committee work stay as they are. When the teacher takes minutes, the meeting is recorded with everyone's consent and a bounded step drafts minutes per agenda item with decisions and owners; the teacher edits them, the chair agrees them, and the teacher checks the agreed version and shares it once.

approvals.approved_version: The minutes with each decision, owner and action point exactly as agreed by the chair and checked by the teacher in s3b, shared once with the meeting's members; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Minutes were typed from handwritten notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting transcription and minute drafting tools.
tasks.still_hard: Meetings where decisions are left vague.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a quiet colleague's view into the meeting.

reach.learn: Whether action points are clearer in drafted minutes.

evidence.claim: Meeting tools transcribe and draft minutes that a person edits.
Recordings that can monitor staff need works council consent where there is one.

assumptions: Boundary: staff meetings and committee work; preparing committee reports is outside.

Input contract for s3: a recording made with all attendees' consent; meetings without consent are minuted by hand (about a third), so s3 keeps 60. Checking and sharing the minutes keep their full time.
Reading papers, meetings and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: How often the teacher takes minutes.

already_counted.description: Adult education teacher edits drafted minutes.

incremental.description: Adult education teacher asks for consent to record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: consent is refused at most meetings, so minutes stay mostly by hand and s3 keeps 80 (1.4); high: about two thirds of meetings recorded as assumed (3.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather the learner's attendance and results, meet with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress, record agreements and follow them up with the learner.

steps.what: Adult education teacher gathers the learner's attendance and test results before the meeting
Adult education teacher meets with other professionals to discuss the student's needs and progress
Adult education teacher records the agreements in the student file
Adult education teacher follows up the agreements with the learner

tasks.design: The student register shows each learner's attendance and test results on one page, so the teacher no longer builds an overview from lists before a meeting with the integration coach or a social worker. Agreements are noted in the student file with a short template. The meetings themselves and follow-up with the learner stay as they are; information is shared outside the school only with the learner's consent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Attendance and results sat in separate lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Student registers with attendance and progress reports.
tasks.still_hard: Learners whose problems lie outside the classroom.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the learner did not say in class.

reach.learn: Whether shared progress pages speed up decisions on extra support.

evidence.claim: Booking and register tools keep attendance and produce attendance reports.
Integration courses need a provider with a certificate or quality mark.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and holding case meetings on a learner; the support given by others is outside.
Input contract for s1: attendance taken by teachers in the register each lesson and test scores entered after each test; learners from other providers have no data in the register.
Meetings and follow-up keep their full time.
Recording agreements is a first record: s3 keeps 85, saving only the layout.
unknowns: How many case meetings per month.
research_questions: Do case meetings get shorter with a progress page?

incremental.description: Adult education teacher records the learner's consent to share information.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many learners come from other providers with no data in the register, so gathering keeps 80 (5.9); high: an integration group with all data in the register (11.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notice learners' attendance or results dropping, guide and counsel students with adjustment or academic problems or special interests, find help or extra materials, note the talk and follow up.

steps.what: Adult education teacher notices learners whose attendance or results drop
Adult education teacher meets the learner to guide and counsel students with adjustment or academic problems or special academic interests
Adult education teacher finds suitable help or extra study materials
Adult education teacher notes the conversation in the student file
Adult education teacher follows up with the student

tasks.design: The student register alerts the teacher when a learner misses a set number of lessons in a row or drops below a set test score; the teacher decides whether to talk. A shared list of local help services and extra materials per level saves searching. Counselling, the note and follow-up stay with the teacher; no software judges or scores learners.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drift showed only when the teacher happened to notice it.
tasks.enabler_now: Register alerts on fixed attendance and score rules.
tasks.still_hard: Learners with problems at home or with residence status.
tasks.human_edge: Building enough trust that a learner says what is wrong.
tasks.altitude: Earlier signals; counselling does not change.

evidence.claim: Register tools keep attendance and produce attendance reports.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes in education institutions is high-risk; the alerts use fixed rules only.

assumptions: Boundary: counselling within the course; professional care is outside.
Input contract for s1: attendance taken by teachers in the register each lesson and test scores entered after tests; alert rules set by the team leader.
The conversation and follow-up keep their full time.
unknowns: How many learners need counselling per course.
research_questions: Do alerts reach learners before they drop out?

incremental.description: Adult education teacher keeps the list of local help services current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small stable groups where the teacher already knows who drops, and the service list rarely fits, so s1 and s3 keep 95 (2.9); high: large integration groups with many absences (8.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
